paragraphs.text: Huangye, 荒野, marks this as leaf picked from uncultivated tea plants growing wild in the mountains of [Anhua](anhua-dark:definition), a county on the Zi river in north-central Hunan whose dark tea is a protected origin product. The wild leaf was then made in the Anhua way, starting as [heimaocha](anhua-dark:making), the one raw tea behind every Anhua tea.

Made in 2024, it is two years old. The slow change in warmth and moisture that makes [dark tea](dark:definition) what it is has only just begun in this leaf. Anhua tea is kept for years and said to improve, though no agreed count of years marks it as [aged](anhua-dark:ageing); kept clean, dry and aired, away from damp and other smells, it has a long way still to go.

brewing.text: In a small pot or gaiwan, use water at the boil and start with a steep of about 15 to 30 seconds, a little longer each round. Pressed and aged Anhua tea is also commonly simmered in a pot.

notice.text: Pine smoke or pine resin above all, a sweet taste and aftertaste, and a mellow, thick, smooth cup; a liquor from yellow and orange to orange-red. Young tea is often smokier in the first infusions and a little bitter, sweetening as the infusions go on.
